story_type: boat rescues from flooded homes during a hurricane
hook: The street was a river, and the rain had not stopped.
narration: This family stepped off their own front stairs and straight into a rescue boat.
Hurricane Isaac had flooded whole neighborhoods along the Mississippi Gulf Coast.
With the rain still pouring, National Guard soldiers went street to street in small boats.
They were from a Special Forces unit, searching flooded neighborhoods for anyone stranded.
Crews use small inflatable boats in floods because they float in shallow water and fit between houses.
Everyone they reached got a life jacket before the boat pulled away.
An older woman rode out sitting low in the boat, soldiers all around her.
At one house, a whole family came down the stairs with whatever they could carry.
[short pause] The soldiers steadied each person as they stepped down into the boat.
outcome: Those soldiers and other Mississippi Guardsmen rescued more than three hundred fifty people from the flood in a few days.
title: Hurricane Isaac flood rescue by boat
description:
After Hurricane Isaac flooded neighborhoods on the Mississippi Gulf Coast in August 2012, Mississippi Army National Guard soldiers searched by boat for stranded residents and brought families out of their flooded homes.

Footage: U.S. Army video by Spc. Michael Needham, 102d Public Affairs Detachment, Mississippi Army National Guard, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/153418/mississippi-national-guard-special-forces-rescue-residents-post-hurricane-isaac
